no gigantic machinery around blocking commands; it is usually not one command but the next ACTION

openIssues.what: No durable session - review_approved (T7 fixed within BA2's own path) included until this finding, and task_run/routine_run/knowledge_action/assistant_turn still today - has its task's own instruction rendered in its prompt. `RunContextBundle` (agent-orchestration/run-orchestration/src/contracts.ts:34-54) carries `taskId` but no description, and `assembleTaskFreePrompt` (provisioner.ts:553-621), the branch every durable session takes because `requestContext` is always set (provisioner.ts:1462-1466 requires `!params.requestContext`), never reads `contextBundle` at all - only `sourceSection`/`conversationSection` built from `params.transcript`. `run-orchestration` may not read the task itself to fill the gap (blind, request-driven executor, architecture.md 2.3/2.6).
sharperEvidenceFromT7RealBinaryRun: BA2's own fix (review-reengagement.ts's buildResumeTranscript) bakes task.title/description into the transcript core-side, and this is PROVEN correct at both levels: the unit test (review/src/__tests__/review-reengagement.integration.test.ts) and a live CLAUDE.md dump from the real-binary lane (local-sb-2/CLAUDE.md) that shows the baked sentence reaching the resumed session's system prompt exactly as designed.

But a task's `description` column is a STANDING field (set once, at task creation) and can never carry a dynamically-generated, session-specific instruction (e.g. an exact file path chosen at runtime). The real-binary test's own fixture (action-gate-realbinary.integration.test.ts:294-326, `seedTaskSessionRequest`) proves this by construction: it seeds `tasks` with no `description` at all, and injects the actual one-shot instruction only into an ephemeral `transcriptBake`/`contextBundle.task.description` scoped to the FIRST session's own AgentSessionRequest - discarded once that session ends. The test file's own comment ('this is what actually gets the instruction in front of the model on the durable path') shows its author already knew task.description would not reach the first session either, without that workaround.

Consequence, reproduced live (haiku, 3/3 attempts across two separate runs): a review_approved-resumed session, even carrying BA2's new task-instruction sentence (title only, no description - ruling 14 correctly declines to invent one), replies 'I appreciate the approval, but I don't have context about what task I was working on or what action was blocked' instead of acting. It is not refusing or suspecting injection - it genuinely lacks the SPECIFIC instruction, because that instruction was never durable.

The real fix for full resumption fidelity is carrying the ORIGINAL blocked session's own instruction/turns forward into the resumed session - a capability distinct from (and larger than) rendering the task's standing description, and touches the same orchestration-layer prompt-assembly code shared by every durable session kind. Out of BA2's scope by the same reasoning as the general case above.
